column11: Which locations or dates recorded the highest pollution levels and what patterns can be observed?
I'll analyze the location information along with the pollution patterns we've already identified.
Location Analysis:

This dataset monitors a single location: Del Norte-2178 in New Mexico (coordinates: 35.1353°N, -106.5847°W). This location is near Albuquerque, New Mexico. The monitoring station tracked 6 pollutants using 6 different sensors over 32 days (December 1, 2025 - January 1, 2026) with 4,284 total measurements.
Since all data comes from one location, the pollution patterns reflect temporal variations rather than geographic differences.
Highest Pollution Dates (Already Identified):
The worst pollution occurred on:
January 1st - Combined PM average of 66.65 µg/m³
December 19th - Combined PM average of 60.87 µg/m³
December 24th - Combined PM average of 49.56 µg/m³
December 18th - Absolute peak of 106 µg/m³ PM10
Weekly Pattern Analysis:
The data shows a clear escalation pattern over the monitoring period:
1. Week of Dec 1-7: Cleanest air - 14.04 µg/m³ combined average
2. Week of Dec 8-14: Moderate increase - 20.9 µg/m³ combined average
3. Week of Dec 15-21: Worst week - 35.74 µg/m³ combined average, peak of 106 µg/m³
4. Week of Dec 22-28: Slight improvement - 28.67 µg/m³ combined average
5. Week of Dec 29-Jan 1: Elevated - 27.76 µg/m³ combined average, highest PM2.5 (39.9 µg/m³)
Key Patterns:
Temporal Escalation: Pollution increased 154% from week 1 to week 3, suggesting either:
Seasonal weather pattern changes (winter inversions)
Accumulation of particulates over time
Holiday-related activities (heating, travel, fireworks)
Holiday Spikes: Both December 24th and January 1st show elevated pollution, likely from:
Increased wood burning for heating
Holiday celebrations and fireworks
Reduced atmospheric mixing during winter
Sensor Performance: All 6 sensors operated consistently throughout the period, with PM10 sensor (3919) recording the most dramatic variations and the absolute peak reading of 106 µg/m³.
The single-location nature of this dataset means all patterns reflect atmospheric and temporal factors at this specific New Mexico site rather than geographic variations
